explanation: [[kw:Open-end credit]] (revolving credit) allows you to borrow repeatedly up to a credit limit, with no fixed number of payments.

explanation: Three common methods to calculate finance charges on credit cards:
- [[kw:Average Daily Balance]]: most common; includes new purchases and payments throughout the cycle.
- [[kw:Previous Balance]]: interest calculated on the balance at the beginning of the billing cycle (does not credit payments made during the cycle).
- [[kw:Adjusted Balance]]: interest calculated on the beginning balance minus any payments made (most favorable to consumers).
The method used appears in the cardholder agreement.
[[imp:For the same balance and APR, the previous balance method yields the highest finance charge, adjusted balance the lowest.]]

notes: Average daily balance is the most common.
Always check your card agreement for the method used.
formulaCard.title: Finance Charge by Method
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Monthly Rate} = \frac{\text{APR}}{12}$$ $$\text{Previous Balance FC} = \text{Previous Balance} \times \text{Monthly Rate}$$ $$\text{Adjusted Balance FC} = (\text{Previous Balance} - \text{Payments}) \times \text{Monthly Rate}$$

teacherCues: Contrast the three methods: average daily balance, previous balance, adjusted balance.

formulaCard.title: Credit Card Finance Charge Blueprint
notes: If method is previous balance, use that instead of average.
If method is adjusted balance, use Previous Balance – Payments.
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Avg Daily Balance} = \frac{\sum (\text{Daily Balance} \times \text{Days})}{\text{Days in Cycle}}$$ $$\text{Finance Charge} = \text{Avg Daily Balance} \times \frac{\text{APR}}{12}$$ $$\text{New Balance} = \text{Previous Balance} + \text{FC} + \text{Purchases} - \text{Payments}$$

explanation: Apply the blueprint to credit card finance charge problems:
1. Understand: identify previous balance, payments, purchases, APR, method (average daily, previous, or adjusted), and billing cycle days.
2. Solve: compute average daily balance (or appropriate base), monthly periodic rate, finance charge, and new balance.
3. Conclude: state the finance charge and new balance; compare to previous balance to see debt trend.
This structured approach ensures you account for all transactions.
